newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Jan 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Jan 21.

text.p: Prepared by The Broadcast Monitoring Company for Reuters
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- HORLICK'S MORGAN GRENFELL COLLEAGUES SPEAK OUT

At least eight of Nicola Horlick's colleagues at Morgan Grenfell said she was seeking to move to ABN Amro Hoare Govett. The Dutch bank is alleged to have planned a weekend poaching of Morgan Grenfell staff, followed by a 385 million pound stg offer for the residual unit trust business.
-- LABOUR PROFIT PLAN ATTACKED

Gas industry regulator Claire Spottiswoode attacks Labour proposals that privatised utilities share 'excess' profits with customers. She says it would lead to utilities attempting to disguise profit levels and harm incentives aimed at reducing costs.
-- BUSINESS PRESSURE GROUPS BACKS MINIMUM WAGE

A new business pressure group, the Business Commission, set up by the Institute for Public Policy and Research, calls for a national minimum wage and expresses support for Britain joining the European Social Chapter and the single currency.
THE TIMES
-- EROSIONAL SEEKS DELAY ON INTEREST

Erosional is seeking an extension of nine months on the interest standstill it forced on banks, due to the Channel Tunnel fire and the delays to services. Executive co-chairman of Erosional, Patrick Ponsolle, is confident that the banks in the syndicate will agree to the request to not start repaying interest on its nine billion pounds stg debt until December.
-- STRONG SALES HELP TESCO TIGHTEN GRIP ON TITLE
Tesco reveals stronger than expected sales in the run-up to Christmas, strengthening its claim to the title of Britain's top supermarket group.
-- PRUDENTIAL TO COMPENSATE PENSION VICTIMS

Britain's biggest insurer, Prudential, is to compensate some of the victims of personal pension mis-selling. The agreement has been reached with the GMB union in return for an end to litigation in the courts.
THE GUARDIAN
-- POUND RETURNS TO ERM LEVEL

Sterling climbs above 2.70 marks for the first time since it left the exchange rate mechanism on Black Wednesday in September 1992, fuelling the policy debate between the Treasury and the Bank of England over the strength of the pound. The strong pound is starting to hurt British exporters, but the expectation of a rise in base rates is helping to increase sterling's strength.
-- PENGUIN JOINS PACK HUNTING REED

Penguin, the publishing group, is believed to be interested in buying of Reed International's consumer books division. Reed Consumer Books was withdrawn from the market a year ago when it failed to attract buyers at a high enough price. The deal would cost Penguin, which is part of the Pearson group, over 100 million pounds stg.
-- REGULATORS CLOSE IN ON CORPORATE FIXERS

City regulators, the Securities and Futures Authority and the Securities and Investments Board are planning a clampdown on unofficial corporate financiers who are not registered with any of the financial watchdogs.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- THORN SHARE PRICE ROCKED BY PROFIT WARNING
Thorn issues a warning that poor trading and the strong pound will hit profits in the year to March, with no more than last year's 170.7 million pounds stg pre-tax profit expected.
-- PRISM DROPS SHARE SCHEME AFTER BIG INVESTORS' PROTEST
Prism Rail responds to shareholder demands and drops a bonus share scheme for its founding shareholders.
-- POST OFFICE CUTS AIMED AT MANAGEMENT

The Post Office announces a 100 million pound stg cost-cutting programme that will hit middle and senior management, in response to competitive pressure in the communications market. A 15-month freeze on the price of stamps is also announced.
